newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australian Broadcasting Corp Afternoon Update.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australian Broadcasting Corp Afternoon Update.

text.p: HEALTH DEPT DEFENDS HANDLING OF SALMONELLA OUTBREAK
Victoria's chief health officer has defended the state health departments handling of an outbreak of salmonella in smallgoods, which has killed two people and left 30 others ill.
Dr Graham Rouch says it has taken some time to establish the source of the outbreak but the department is more than happy with their investigation.
The department has linked the outbreak to ham and silverside manufactured Melbourne smallgoods company Lago.
Doctor Rouch says negotiations went on yesterday and the company is distancing itself, although it is co-operating with the recall in Tasmania, Victoria, South Australia and Queensland.
Two Victorians, a 79-year-old man and an 86-year-old-woman, died several weeks ago and 30 Victorians and South Australians are ill after eating contaminated meat.
STATES WARY OF GOVT'S GREEN COMMITMENT
The Federal Government's been warned against linking its billion-dollar commitment to the environment to spending by the states.
The money will be raised by the partial sell-off of Telstra.
But South Australian premier John Olsen says there are disturbing indications the Federal Government might seek a matching commitment from the States.
He's told the Premiers' Conference in Canberra this would undermine efforts to improve Commonwealth-State financial relations.
PREMIERS WANT HEALTH SYSTEM REVIEWED
The States and Territories want the Prime Minister to agree to an external review of the health system, as dissatisfaction with the health system becomes an issue at the Premiers' Conference.
The States are unhappy with the Federal Government's health direction and if the Prime Minister refuses to agree, the States may commission the review themselves.
The Premiers conference is continuing in Canberra.
CYCLONE JUSTIN MOVES TOWARDS QLD COAST
Tropical cyclone Justin is continuing to move towards the north Queensland coast at about 12 kilometres an hour.
It's currently located 280 kilometres east of Cooktown and is moving west-south-west.
The Cyclone Warning Centre expects it'll cross the coast mid tomorrow morning.
SOFT DRINK BOTTLE CLOSES SYDNEY STREETS
Sydney's streets were blocked for half an hour this afternoon over a can of soft drink.
Police say an employee at the Air New Zealand building in Elizabeth Street, called them to say a soft drink can with Semtex written on it, had been left on a shelf.
Police treated it as suspicious, evacuated the building and sent in the bomb disposal sqaud.
The can has now been found to be an overseas brank of soft drink.
BEACON RECOVERED
Searchers have recovered debris along with a second emergency positioning beacon, from a yacht New Zealand missing in the Coral Sea.
The debris was picked up by HMAS Melbourne, but it's so far failed to give any significant clues in the search for the crew of the Queen Charlotte.
Four aircraft and six vessels are searching a six-thousand square nautical-mile area off North Queensland for the five crew members.
Search co-ordinator Daryl Hiron, says searchers are still hopeful of finding survivors, and are working on the theory they may have got away on a life-craft.
NIGEL THOMPSON WINS ARCHIBALD PRIZE
Nigel Thomson has won this year's Archibald Prize, with a portrait of writer, Barbara Blackman.
The winner was announced a short time ago at the Art Gallery of New South Wales.
